Raw hex address 0x4a2e6b assigned to bare local `uVar11`. The decompiler dropped a symbolic reference — either a data-symbol pointer (recover the symbol from the .asm and replace `uVar11` with symbolic global/array indexing, §11) or a dead code-address store from return-address tracking (delete it, §14). Magic addresses do not survive the relink.

Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (countdown for-loop with the `(uint)bool * -N + M` direction idiom — Watcom's REP MOVSD lowering fingerprint). Replace the whole loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * stride) or a struct assignment in a .keep.

Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.
